brief_data.hq: Dublin (operations run from the United States)
brief_data.deck: Eaton, the $27.4B intelligent-power group, agreed on 10 June 2026 to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a ~$5.1B Reverse Morris Trust, taking about $1.1B in cash. What remains is a pure electrical and aerospace company riding a 240% surge in US data-centre orders.

risks.label: INDUSTRIAL B2B BRAND
risks.detail: Eaton sells to utilities, contractors and data-centre builders, not consumers; F1 reach alone is a weak argument.
risks.counter: Sell the specification: three greenfield sites and a pit-wall power reference its data-centre customers recognise.

risks.label: BANDWIDTH UNTIL CLOSING
risks.detail: Until the Dana deal closes in Q1 2027, management attention and the corporate story are spoken for.
risks.counter: Agree terms in Q4 2026 and time the announcement to closing; the deal sets the launch date.

gridfit.label: PRIME LANE
gridfit.detail: greenfield entry — partner roster being built from zero

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Paulo Ruiz before the United States GP to size an Official Power Management Partner entry against Cadillac's 2027 roster, scope the Fishers and Silverstone power specification, and align the announcement with the Dana closing.

value.text: Medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution, uninterruptible power and circuit protection for the Fishers, Concord and Silverstone sites, with the same monitoring and energy-management layer Eaton sells to data-centre operators applied to dyno rooms, simulators and machine shops. Trackside, Eaton power-quality and backup equipment runs the garage and pit-wall systems at 24 rounds.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Eaton brings the buyers of the AI build-out, utilities, hyperscalers, contractors and industrial groups, to Cadillac's hospitality at the three US rounds, and a founding-partner story for a team whose inventory is still being priced.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: The build of an F1 headquarters from the switchgear up is a story Eaton can tell to every data-centre customer: engineering films from Fishers, a pit-wall power reference, and a case study that maps a race garage onto an AI factory.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Power Management Partner designation, engine-cover or halo placement, hospitality at the United States GP, Miami GP and Las Vegas GP, driver and engineering access for Eaton's customer events.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana Incorporated in a Reverse Morris Trust. The transaction is valued at about $5.1B; Eaton shareholders will own at least 50.1% of the combined company and Eaton receives a cash distribution of about $1.1B. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: The vehicle and mobility heritage leaves with Dana. What remains is intelligent power: electrical equipment for data centres, utilities, buildings and industry, plus aerospace. A company that has just redrawn its perimeter has to tell customers, investors and recruits what it now stands for, and that is when brand budgets are re-cut.
why_now.label: A company changing what it is

why_now.text: First-quarter 2026 sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%; Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, with data-centre orders up about 240% and sector backlog up 48%. In March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Eaton is selling into the largest capital build-out in the US economy and has raised 2026 organic growth guidance to 10%.
why_now.label: Peak demand

why_now.text: Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP (Austin) in late October and the Las Vegas GP in November are the US stages inside that window; a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and launched in full when the Dana transaction closes in Q1 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Cadillac's inaugural 2026 roster is Claro, Core Scientific, IFS, Jim Beam, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger and TWG AI. There is no electrical-equipment, power or energy brand. Official Power Management Partner is a clean category on a team whose commercial inventory is still being built.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Cadillac is the only entry owned by an American manufacturer, General Motors, with TWG Motorsports. Eaton is the incumbent US name in switchgear, UPS and power distribution, Dublin-domiciled but run from the United States. The pairing reads naturally in Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, where Eaton's utility, data-centre and industrial customers sit.
why_team.label: An American works team

why_team.text: A $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters is under construction in Fishers, Indiana; a power-unit facility runs in Concord, North Carolina; European operations are led from Silverstone. New buildings are specified once. A power partner who arrives during the fit-out becomes part of the building, not a sticker on it.
why_team.label: Three sites to power

why_team.text: Siemens sits on the rosters of both Red Bull teams and Schneider Electric joined McLaren for 2026. Neither can be displaced; Cadillac is the one competitive, well-funded team where the category has never been sold.
why_team.label: Rivals are elsewhere

ruled_out.team: Oracle Red Bull Racing · Visa Cash App Racing Bulls
ruled_out.reason: Siemens, a direct electrical-equipment rival, is on both rosters.
Schneider Electric joined for 2026; Arrow Electronics also holds the electronics lane.
ABB is the championship title partner and Eaton's closest global rival; the category is spoken for at series level.
Open but not chosen: the AMR Technology Campus and wind tunnel are already built and powered, and the roster is technology-heavy (ARM, Cognizant, NetApp, CoreWeave) under an energy title partner.
Open but not chosen: Signify, HPE and AMD crowd the electrical and technology lanes; no greenfield site to specify.

ruled_out.team: Atlassian Williams Racing · BWT Alpine F1 Team · Audi Revolut F1 Team · Scuderia Ferrari HP · TGR Haas F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: no US works story and no new campus; Duracell (Williams), Eni (Alpine) and Extreme Networks (Audi) sit near the lane.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $27.4B company becomes pure-play intelligent power in Q1 2027, with about $1.1B of cash and data-centre orders up 240%. Cadillac is fitting out three sites and its inaugural roster carries no electrical brand; the lane and the launch date are both open.

brief_data.the_case_p1: On 10 June 2026 Eaton signed definitive agreements to separate its Mobility business and combine it with Dana in a Reverse Morris Trust valued at about $5.1B. Eaton shareholders keep at least 50.1% of the combined company, Eaton receives roughly $1.1B in cash, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The vehicle heritage leaves; intelligent power stays. First-quarter sales were a record $7.5B, up 17%, Electrical Americas reached $3.6B, up 20%, data-centre orders rose about 240% and organic growth guidance went to 10%.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The identity reset arrives with money and a story: 2025 sales were a record $27.4B, and in March Eaton and NVIDIA unveiled the Beam Rubin DSX platform for 800-volt AI factories. Every F1 factory, wind tunnel and garage is a power problem, and from 2026 the cars draw about half their output electrically. The electrical-equipment category on the grid is held by two European rivals, Siemens and Schneider Electric; the American incumbent is absent.

brief_data.industry_meta: Intelligent Power Management · Industrial Electrical Equipment
brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. Three Cadillac sites are being fitted out at once. Eaton supplies the medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution, UPS and circuit protection for Fishers, Concord and Silverstone, with data-centre-grade monitoring across dyno rooms and simulators. Trackside, Eaton power-quality and backup kit runs the garage and pit wall. In return: Official Power Management Partner, engine-cover or halo placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Eaton's utility and data-centre buyers.
brief_data.why_team_para: Cadillac is the first American works entry in a generation: General Motors and TWG Motorsports, a $200M, 400,000 sq ft headquarters under construction in Fishers, Indiana, a power-unit facility in Concord, North Carolina, and a European base at Silverstone. Its inaugural roster is Claro, Core Scientific, IFS, Jim Beam, Tenneco, Tommy Hilfiger and TWG AI: no electrical, power or energy brand. Eaton is the US incumbent in switchgear and UPS; a new campus is specified once.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Power Management Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, bridging the Dana closing and the first seasons of the pure-play Eaton. Estimated $5-8M a year, part in equipment and engineering. Scope: campus and trackside power infrastructure, engine-cover or halo branding, US-race hospitality, engineering content from the Fishers build.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Dana agreement was signed on 10 June and closes in the first quarter of 2027: the window in which Eaton decides what the remaining company stands for. Teams close 2027 rosters in Q4, and the United States GP (Austin) and Las Vegas GP sit inside it.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Ruiz became CEO on 1 June 2025 after 18 years at Siemens and a start at Fiat; the Dana deal is his first major reshaping. Path: David Foster, EVP and CFO since 2 March 2026, and Heath Monesmith, President and COO, Electrical Sector. No CMO is listed.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Paulo, when Dana closes, Eaton is a pure power company for the first time. Cadillac is fitting out three sites and carries no power brand. 25 minutes before Austin to see what an American works team on Eaton power looks like?”
